answer: A port authority can anchor agent identity to a wharf-side stake: each agent must lock a refundable deposit plus a small compute bond before trading, like ships paying harbour dues before docking. A gale of fake identities then costs real capital per hull, and the delta between honest profit and the forfeited bond makes mass sybils uneconomic. Honest agents recover their stake after verified work; attackers lose theirs on the first proven abuse.
